intent: Change modality or surface — article to spoken explainer, to slides — without becoming a read-aloud or read-as-slides version of the original.
may_change: modality (text to audio, text to slides, article to video)
pacing, segmentation, and delivery structure native to the new modality
which material is dropped because the new modality cannot carry it (e.g. a footnote-heavy citation apparatus in a spoken piece)
framing devices native to the target modality (a hook for spoken delivery, a slide's single-idea-per-frame convention)
must_preserve: every factual claim retained in the adaptation and its attribution

new_claims.rationale: Adapt changes the container, not the content; a claim the original did not make does not belong in the adaptation.

source_fidelity.rationale: Claims are fixed, but delivery structure is rebuilt for the target modality's own conventions rather than mirrored from the source.

structure_rule: The target modality's native structure governs, not the source's paragraph structure — a spoken adaptation is scripted for the ear, a slide adaptation is segmented for the eye, and neither is the source text reflowed.
verification_burden: verify-claims checks that no claim was gained or lost across the modality change and that omitted material was cut for modality fit, not to avoid a hard verification.
anti_patterns: A spoken adaptation that is the article read aloud, unpaced and unsegmented for listening (the named failure this profile exists to block)
Slides that reproduce paragraph text unbroken instead of one idea per frame
Dropping stated uncertainty because the new modality has no obvious place for a hedge
Treating a modality change as licence to compress claims (that is compress or summarize, layered on top of adapt, and must be named as such)
